gh pr create --base main --title "APRV-386: one script provisions the three demo instances, idempotently" --body-file - <<'BODY'
## What

The web-agent demo, its crowd track and the Grok Bot connector demo were each provisioned by pasting a command sequence out of a runbook. `examples/demo-provision.mjs` is that sequence, detected before it is run, so that a rehearsal starts from a known state and a reset is one line instead of a re-read.

```sh
node examples/demo-provision.mjs --instance web-agent      # ~/demo-gate
node examples/demo-provision.mjs --instance guest          # ~/demo-guest, the crowd track
node examples/demo-provision.mjs --instance grok-bot       # the Grok Bot connector demo
```

Plus `--path <dir>`, `--check`, `--reset [--vault]`, `--json`.

**One script, not three.** The demos differ only in data (the path, which steps are human-only, which ports they may bind, what is seeded); the idempotency, the stop-at-a-human-step and the reset logic are identical, and three copies would drift the way the three runbooks already had.

## The properties, and where they are pinned

| Property | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Writes inside the instance and nowhere else | the parent directory is listed before and after every run |
| A second run overwrites nothing (bytes **and** mtimes) | `a second run overwrites nothing and still exits 0` |
| An `APPROVAL.md` it did not scaffold is KEPT (overwriting an attested policy refuses every gate verb with `hash-mismatch`) | `an existing policy that differs is kept, never overwritten` |
| No human-only step is ever run: after a full provision there is no `events.jsonl` at all | `the script runs no human-only step` |
| `--reset` retires the previous log whole into `<instance>/retired/<stamp>/`, byte for byte, and never truncates | `--reset retires the log instead of truncating it, and keeps the vault` |
| The vault survives a reset; `--vault` retires it | two tests |
| The guest instance holds no credential (runbook §4's MUST): the vault and adapter steps are refused, and `--check` FAILS if one appears | `the guest instance is refused a vault, and --check fails if one appears` |
| The packaged policy is the block `provisioning.md` explains | `the packaged demo policy is the one provisioning.md publishes` |

Every step it runs is a documented verb — `approval init`, `approval payload hash`, `approval policy check`, and `approval doctor --json` / `approval env --check --json` for state detection. No log line is hand-written, nothing inside `.approval/` is edited, and no real credential appears anywhere in the change. The tests drive the real script against scratch instances built through the real verbs.

`approval policy attest`, `setup identity`, `setup vault`, `setup channel telegram`, the mail adapter verb and the Grok demo's repository clone are printed as fully-qualified lines and left for a human; the clone is printed first and nothing is scaffolded until it is done, because a clone refuses a directory that already holds files.

## Two decisions worth review

1. **`grok-bot` and `web-agent` both name `~/demo-gate`.** A `demo-instance.json` marker records which demo a directory was provisioned for; a mismatch refuses at exit 2 and names the two ways out (`--path`, `--reset`); an unmarked existing directory (Carter's `~/demo-gate` from 2026-08-30) is adopted rather than refused.
2. **The crowd track's MUST said "steps 1, 2 and 3, and stop there" and then named only two forbidden verbs.** The script refuses exactly those two (`setup vault`, the mail adapter) for the guest instance, and still prints `setup identity` and `setup channel telegram` — they hold no credential of that instance's own and are what put a guest's request on the phone. The runbook now says so.

## Docs

`examples/web-agent-demo/provisioning.md`, both runbooks and a new `examples/README.md` ("Reproducing a demo") reference the script instead of repeating the sequence, keeping the prose that explains why. The demo policy moves out of the heredoc into `examples/policies/demo-gate.APPROVAL.md` so a policy change is a diff; `tests/demo-guest-limits.test.ts` still extracts the block from `provisioning.md` and still passes.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` clean. `node scripts/run-tests.mjs --only demo-provision`: 16/16.

Full `npm test` locally: **4809 tests, 4786 pass, 22 fail** — all 22 are the pre-existing local SMTP/TLS suites (`adapter-email`, `smtp-probe`, `setup-adapter-email`) that fail on this machine's Node v26. CI on Node 22 is the truth for those.

Closes APRV-386.
